segments.text: The Qur'an once described the most arrogant man in Makkah... by a single patch of his body. Not his heart. Not his tongue. The front of his head... and it called that patch a liar.
segments._shot: harsh shadow of a lone figure on a wall, abstract, no face

segments.text: This is the verse... of the lying forelock.
segments.title: THE FORELOCK
segments._shot: slow smoke curling through a shaft of dark red light

segments.text: Meet the man first. Abu Jahl... a chief of Makkah, and the fiercest enemy the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, ever had. The Prophet would pray openly at the Ka'bah, the ancient sanctuary at the heart of the city... and Abu Jahl swore before his people that if he saw him pray again, he would trample his neck.
segments._shot: REDO: fire against a dark stone wall (Pexels 34230599)

segments.text: And the answer came down from heaven, in the very chapter whose first word was Read. No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock... a lying, sinning forelock.
segments._shot: fist of storm cloud dragging across a dark sky

segments.text: The forelock is the front of the head, where the hair falls over the brow. To be dragged by it was total humiliation... the proud head, seized from the front. And the classical scholars explain the description... lying in its statements, sinful in its actions... the forelock standing for the man himself.
segments._shot: REDO: dark turbulent dusk sky + crescent (dust-storm stand-in) (Pexels 36738426)

segments.text: Some readers today pause at a further layer... that behind the forehead sits the part of the brain most tied to planning, choice, and deceit. Take that as a quiet reflection, not as the verse's claim... the tafsir needed no anatomy. The Qur'an aimed at the seat of arrogance... and arrogance has an address.
segments._shot: close texture of furrowed stone, brooding light

segments.text: As for Abu Jahl... he never did trample that neck. He died at Badr, the first great battle, defeated by the people he had tortured... a humiliation as public as his threat had been.
segments._shot: REDO: empty quiet desert plain at dusk (Pexels 6010313)

segments.text: The forelock is where pride lives... the head you refuse to lower. Muslims touch theirs to the ground, on purpose, many times a day. The question the verse leaves behind... is what your forehead bows to.
segments._shot: REDO: empty mosque archway with red prayer carpet (Pexels 37320224)
